topic.title: How the jewellery shop makes money on a ₹1 lakh Dhanteras necklace: the making charge

title: Your Dhanteras necklace: how the jeweller really earns 💍
description:
Why is your gold bill more than the gold? Here's where the jewellery shop really makes its money.
A ₹1 lakh necklace with an assumed 10% making charge, computed: what you pay on top, and what you don't get back when you sell. No jeweller named; the charge is an example, not a rule. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Did you check your making charge? Comment

lines.text: This gold is worth ₹1,00,000. So why is my bill ₹1.1 L?
Making charges. An assumed 10% on top of the gold.
Gold sells at the day's rate. Every shop pays it. The making charge is where the shop earns.
Fine. One day I'll sell it and get it all back.
When you sell, shops usually pay for the gold only. That ₹10,000? Gone.
So ask for the making charge first. Because this gold...

No sourced facts. Topic verify list met: no jeweller named, making charge said as 'an assumed 10%', GST not mentioned. Claims hold for India: gold priced at the day's rate, making charge on top, buyers of old jewellery usually pay for gold only. Disclaimer ends the description, no product advice. Notes: the real bill also carries 3% GST (about ₹1.13 L, still ₹1.1 L rounded); the making charge also pays for labour, so 'where the shop earns' simplifies a little.
